posts.author: 0x00EB
posts.body:
Hi everyone,
I’ve been working on a simple, browser-based tileset editor and wanted to share it here.
It’s completely free and runs directly in your browser:
Tileset Lab by 0x00EB
A browser-based tool for creating and editing tileset images
0x00eb.itch.io
The goal is to make assembling and reorganizing tilesets quick and painless, especially for RPG Maker users.
Features:
Runs in your browser
No downloads, no installation, no platform limitations.
Fully customizable grid system
Define any grid size to match your engine or personal workflow.
Built-in RPG Maker grid presets
Native support for RPG Maker tilesets: A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, B, C, D, and E.
Multiple source images
Combine tiles from multiple images into a single tileset.
Instant export
Export and download your tileset image with a single click.
Undo / redo support
Experiment freely without worrying about mistakes.
The tool is still evolving, so feedback and suggestions are very welcome.

posts.author: Coolie
posts.body:
Using Mozilla Firefox 146.0.1, I gave it a test, and after a few minutes of messing around, I hit export and nothing happens. If that isn't expected behavior, this may require a certain browser. What browser was it made for?
Edit: After a few reloads of Firefox, it downloaded the edited tileset correctly, so I guess... Firefox users just be aware?

posts.author: 0x00EB
posts.body:
Thanks a lot for testing my tool! During development, I mainly tested it in Chrome. I’ve now tested it in Firefox as well and was able to reproduce the download issue. -> It should be fixed now.
One thing to note: to see the tileset being downloaded, I had to open the browser’s download panel. Otherwise, there was no visible indication in the UI that a file download was in progress.

posts.author: Coolie
posts.body:
0x00EB said:
One thing to note: to see the tileset being downloaded, I had to open the browser’s download panel. Otherwise, there was no visible indication in the UI that a file download was in progress.
Click to expand...
Yeah, after I saved a few times, I went and changed settings to always choose where to download files, rather than automatically send them to the download folder. That helps to give more of an indication to the user that a file is being saved. But in either environment, it seems to work just fine. Nice work on this!
